Researchers asked anxious people to write down their worries for ten days.
Then, for a month, they checked which worries came true.
And a third of the ones that did turned out better than expected.
So why does your mind keep replaying the worst case?
If I think about it enough, nothing can hurt me.
But you've replayed that scene a hundred times. Nothing changed.
Here's how to break the loop.
Anxious students who wrote about their worries before an exam scored higher.
Two. Give your worries an appointment.
Fifteen minutes each evening. Until then, they wait.
Three. Ask yourself: can I act on this today?
If yes, take one small step. If not, let it go for now.
Your thoughts are not facts. They're weather. They pass.
Most of what you fear will never come.
Right now, write down one worry. Then close the notebook.
